svg.title: P025 · Customer sign-ups by year and quarter
svg.desc: One row per sign-up year and quarter. IDs 2 and 3 both map to 2025 Q1. ID 4 maps to Q2. ID 5 has NULL year and quarter. The five customer IDs form four groups. IDs 2 and 3 count together, and ID 5 contributes one to the missing-date group. The three dated groups run chronologically, followed by NULL / NULL. Counts 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 recover all five customers.
svg.text: Customer sign-ups by year and quarter
One row per sign-up year and quarter.
Where do March 31, April 1 and a missing sign-up date go?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
What quarter does each customer enter?
IDs 2 and 3 both map to 2025 Q1. ID 4 maps to Q2. ID 5 has NULL year and quarter.
CAST(strftime('%Y', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) / CASE WHEN … THEN 1 … END AS signup_quarter
Which keys must be grouped together?
The five customer IDs form four groups. IDs 2 and 3 count together, and ID 5 contributes one to the missing-date
Where should the missing-date group appear?
The three dated groups run chronologically, followed by NULL / NULL. Counts 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 recover all five
ORDER BY signup_year ASC NULLS LAST, signup_quarter ASC NULLS LAST
